decision: STANDS, with the provenance sub-claim OPEN. The supporting reports are verifiers 0 (refute) and 1 (rederive) on the grade, the audit on every number, and verifier 2 (data) on every data row. Verifier 2's NARROWED repeats the audit's narrowing argument and never takes up the necessary-condition reading, so it is not followed on the grade. (1) Every number re-runs. The audit script, copied to adjudicate/run/crs_rederive.py, exits 0 with output md5 f80851f3d228d7d151f3bc44ad7b9ed4, the same as the audit's. It has 33 PASS lines, not 34. Re-running verifier 0's crs_refute.py gives md5 e5f555843097e4843263263192cd0fa6, the same as theirs. wall.py --selftest prints SELFTEST OK, and wall.matter_crossover() = 0.4689765563942486 = (17 - sqrt33)/24. (2) The NARROWED argument is that 0.46898 holds only for one speed, and the K7 alternatives give lower crossovers. I now prove exactly what verifiers 0 and 1 found only by random search (adjudicate/run/crs_jensen.py, output md5 49a6dc9a70b63bc0db7f14b23276fbb3). Take any speed distribution at one radius, with each particle conserving its own L (u_i ~ 1/R) and n ~ 1/R^2. Sympy gives, identically, d sigma_i/dR = -(2/R)(sigma_i + p_i), which is per-component Israel conservation, and d p_i/dR = -(2/R)(2 p_i - sigma_i v_i^4/4). Hence beta^2_mix = (2p - (1/4) sum sigma_i v_i^4)/(sigma + p). At fixed Lanczos statics (sigma, p), beta^2_single - beta^2_mix = sigma Var_sigma(v^2) / (4 (sigma + p)), which is >= 0 and zero only for a single speed (Jensen). The single-speed form reduces symbolically to wall.py:86. The same formula reproduces the audit's thin-cluster crossover 0.447387 and margin 1.133151. The single-speed margin crosses 1 only once in (0, 8/9) (K6). So any distribution with the same statics clears the threshold only at x where a single speed does, that is x < (17 - sqrt33)/24. wall.py:98-99, 'counter-rotating matter clears the threshold only for x < 0.46898', is therefore TRUE as written for the whole class the audit widened it to. The audit's alternatives (0.447387, 0.445357, 0.430510, and below 0.1) are instances of that bound, not narrowings of it. (3) The other reading is that 0.46898 is also the sufficiency boundary. That holds for the tree's model, whose single speed is stated in the formula (sigma = n mu gamma with one gamma, p = n mu gamma v^2/2, wall.py:81). The single speed is also forced in a strictly distributional shell if each particle feels the mean extrinsic curvature: verifier 0's R1, re-run here, gives v^2 = (1-s)/(2s) for every particle, difference 0. That mean-geometry law is a NAMED hypothesis, NAMED-NOT-READ, and the grade does not rest on it. Under the other idealisation, the thin limit of an Einstein cluster, sufficiency fails only on (0.447387, 0.468977). That number itself comes from a rigid L-conserving trial motion (verifier 1, point 4), so it is a trial-mode result. The tree asserts no point in that interval. Every point it does assert holds under both idealisations, as the audit itself computed: x = 0.3 stable (1.144558 single speed, 1.133151 cluster), x = 0.4 stable, x = 2/3 and 4/5 unstable, the margin tends to 4/3 as x -> 0, and designpoint.py:160-161's 1/6 lies below both crossovers. (4) No datum enters. The result is closed-form in x, so DATA-DEPENDENT does not apply. Verifier 2 confirmed every data row independently: mpmath root 0.468976556394248805839557855491, table rows to 6 decimals, and the cluster statics to 1e-29. (5) Over-representation was checked both ways. Grading NARROWED would charge the tree with a class-wide claim that is in fact class-wide true. Grading STANDS does not credit the tree with more than it shows: the bound is proven here, not by the tree; the single-speed hypothesis is carried only by the formula; and the provenance claim stays OPEN.
scope: Covered: the radial (l = 0) stability of a thin shell of collisionless counter-rotating particles, Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside, under these NAMED hypotheses. H1: a distributional shell with Lanczos statics p0/sigma0 = (1-s)/(4s). H2: tangential motion isotropic on the 2-sphere at one common speed, as stated by sigma = n mu gamma; under H1 plus H-mean it is forced. H-mean: particles of a strictly thin shell feel the mean extrinsic curvature. NAMED-NOT-READ; the grade does not depend on it. H3: each particle conserves its own L under a spherically symmetric (rigid) radial perturbation. H4: stability judged by beta^2 = dp/dsigma along that sequence, against beta^2_crit (audited separately), and also tested by the EOM in K5 without beta^2_crit. Under these the grade covers: the beta^2_vlasov formula and its 1/2 ceiling; the 8/9 expiry; the crossover (17 - sqrt33)/24 = 0.468976556; the four table rows; the 1.144557648 margin; the 4/3 limit; and the stated conclusion 'clears the threshold only for x < 0.46898'. That conclusion is proven true as a necessary condition for ANY speed distribution with the same statics, and is exact as an iff for the single-speed model. Not covered: (a) the provenance claim 'no member or paper states it in this form' (wall.py:77-78). It is OPEN because no literature search ran, and alphaXiv discovery was not re-attempted here. (b) Non-radial (l >= 2) stability of a kinetic shell. The tree's import of PSP's perfect-fluid instability at wall.py:119-128 is an adjacent, separate finding. (c) Sufficiency of 0.46898 under the thick-shell-limit (Einstein-cluster) idealisation. There the crossover is 0.447387 under a rigid trial mode, which is itself not a full equilibrium analysis. (d) Ames-Andreasson-Logg and LeMaitre-Poisson 2019 remain NAMED-NOT-READ.

Dadhich's 'v^2 = 8/9' (2504.00064v2 p.7, cached text lines 270-287) does not come from the AAL limit 2p_t/rho -> 1. It is his own relativistic virial relation (cached text lines 70-90: 'limiting compactness, M/R = 4/9 for massive particles with velocity, v^2 = 8/9'). For a single-speed 2D gas 2p_t/rho = v^2, so 2p_t/rho -> 1 means local v -> 1. That is consistent with the tree's expiry at x = 2M/R = 8/9. The discrepancy is internal to Dadhich and is recorded as such, not against the tree.

K7a's thin-cluster crossover 0.447387 rests on a hypothesis the audit did not name: a rigid L-conserving trial motion in which each layer leaves its own circular-orbit equilibrium (verifier 1, point 4). A trial-mode V'' > 0 does not prove stability.

The K7c rest-dominated mixtures cannot be realized under either idealisation. In a strictly thin shell under the mean-geometry law every particle has v^2 = (1-s)/(2s). In the thin-cluster limit the speed map v^2(q) = q/(2(1-q)) with uniform dm is fixed. They are not refutations, as the audit already says.
The provenance sub-claim 'no member or paper states it in this form' stays OPEN, untested.
